sources.title: README.md
sources.locator: Features; Getting Started; OpenCode V2; Requirements
sources.finding: Electron and Tauri desktop clients on three OSes and standalone npm server. OpenCode shared service owns execution and sessions. Git worktrees, remote access, browser previews, MCP and plugin controls are described.

sources.title: docs/help/en/missions.md
sources.locator: Create then explicitly start; Follow the tree; Launch criteria; Controls and recovery
sources.finding: Durable paused missions have coordinator/delegates, dependency task trees, reports, explicit start, schedules/events and separate pause, interrupt and terminal stop controls. Native schedules require experimental.schedules and supported OpenCode.

sources.title: docs/help/en/providers.md
sources.locator: Connect; Select and manage accounts; Automatic selection limits; Usage
sources.finding: Native OpenCode OAuth/API-key connections and service-wide saved accounts are supported. Codex subscription OAuth and OpenCode Claude Pro/Max OAuth are distinguished from Claude Code login. Usage quotas and cost estimates are not bills.

sources.title: docs/help/en/mobile.md
sources.locator: Connect; PWA; Capability and connectivity limits
sources.finding: Phone/tablet browser and PWA can operate the reachable backend. No offline backend; closing PWA leaves standalone backend running, while quitting host desktop backend disables Remote Control.

sources.title: docs/help/en/permissions.md
sources.finding: Permission dock exposes native OpenCode requests; actions retain native scope. UI distinguishes permission responses from already-running shell/tool cancellation.

sources.title: PRIVACY.md
sources.finding: CodeNomad says it has no product accounts, telemetry, analytics or advertising. Local projects/conversations/settings remain on host; OpenCode sends content to configured providers. Release/UI update and package requests remain.

sources.title: v1.0.1-dev-20261108-175b1820
sources.finding: v1.0.1-dev-20261108-175b1820 was published 2026-11-08. Release notes describe the scoped changes; this is not a hands-on check.

sources.title: CodeNomad README
sources.locator: Getting started ('connect your model provider'); footer licence line
sources.finding: The user connects their own model provider; the README states no price and marks the project MIT-licensed.

sources.title: CodeNomad LICENSE
sources.finding: The MIT license grants permission to use, copy, modify and distribute the software free of charge.

sources.title: Download CodeNomad
sources.locator: Page header and Desktop apps section (version 1.0.1)
sources.finding: The download page describes CodeNomad as a free and open-source (MIT) desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux and offers installers for version 1.0.1; it shows no price or paid plan.

sources.title: CodeNomad README, installation
sources.locator: README.md lines 38-70 (desktop and standalone server installation) and line 245 (MIT licence footer), release v1.0.1 commit 3e9cbb1
sources.finding: Desktop builds download from the releases page and the standalone server runs on the user's host; the README names no price, account or paid plan and marks the project MIT licensed.

sources.finding: CodeNomad v1.0.1 is an OpenCode workspace. Its Antigravity references exercise provider usage handling, not a separate Antigravity CLI launch.
